narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Ukasar-ukasar sounds like two, so I write the first number twice. That makes ukasar written nine times.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Look at the pebbles again. Ukasar-ukasar is two pairs, which is four pebbles in all.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Multiplying by it means writing the first number four times, not two.

narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>To check, turn each Gumulgal number into our numbers and work the sum.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Nine plus seven is sixteen, and sixteen is eight twos, so the first one matches.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer card; check lines: 9 + 7 = 16, 9 − 6 = 3, 9 × 4 = 36, 16 ÷ 4 = 4

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu reads ukasar-ukasar as two and writes the first number only twice, getting ukasar written nine times. Ukasar-ukasar is two twos, which is four, so the number must be written four times.
